one_liner: C library of brokerless messaging patterns (PUB/SUB, REQ/REP, etc.) with lower small-message latency than ZeroMQ on one host.
what_it_does: nanomsg is the original ZeroMQ author's C rewrite of brokerless messaging. It implements 'scalability protocols' (PAIR, REQ/REP, PUB/SUB, PIPELINE push/pull, SURVEY, BUS) over inproc, IPC (Unix domain sockets on POSIX), TCP and WebSocket transports. The API is shaped like POSIX sockets: sockets are plain ints from nn_socket(AF_SP, NN_PUB) and are used with nn_bind/nn_connect/nn_send/nn_recv, there is no context object, and nn_allocmsg with NN_MSG hands library-owned buffers across instead of copying into caller buffers. It is not a drop-in for libzmq, because the function names, socket options and wire protocol (SP, with an 8-byte \0SP header) all differ, but PUB/SUB and REQ/REP map one-to-one, so porting is mostly mechanical.
how_it_is_fast: It is plain C that uses intrusive containers to keep allocations per message low. nn_chunkref stores payloads of 32 bytes or less (usually protocol headers) inline. PUB fan-out (nn_dist_send) shares one reference-counted chunk across all subscriber pipes instead of copying the body for each subscriber. SUB sockets match subscriptions against a memory-compact Patricia trie with sparse and dense child nodes, and the library avoids ZeroMQ's double buffering (a user-space queue plus the kernel buffer) by relying on the transport's own buffers. It is not zero-copy, though: the inproc transport still memcpys each message once, and all async I/O runs on a single internal epoll/kqueue worker thread (src/aio/pool.c). That keeps CPU and memory low for small messages but limits how far it scales with large payloads and many subscribers.
when_to_use: Same-host PUB/SUB or request/reply with small-to-medium messages (about 1-64 KB in-process, up to 128 KB over IPC), where mean latency and CPU matter more than peak throughput. The SRDS 2025 study measured a 1 KB mean of 7.5 vs 10.3 us in-process and 16.2 vs 25.8 us over IPC against ZeroMQ.
CPU- or memory-constrained hosts. It is ANSI C89 with no C++ runtime, and the study found it had the lowest CPU at every IPC message size and the lowest memory use of ZeroMQ, nanomsg and NNG.
Designs that want SURVEY (surveyor/respondent) or BUS as built-in socket types, or REQ sockets with built-in request retry, rather than building these on top of ZeroMQ primitives.
Existing nanomsg deployments, or peers that must speak the SP wire protocol, including NNG, which upstream says is wire-compatible.
when_not_to_use: New projects. Upstream says the library is in 'sustaining' mode: new features have stopped and only severe defects are fixed. It points users to NNG, which it says is API-compatible for about 99% of apps.

TCP with 16-64 KB messages at default settings. In the study, mean latency at 16-32 KB was about 560 us vs ZeroMQ's 40 us. NN_TCP_NODELAY defaults to 0 (Nagle on), and upstream closed the request to change that default (#674) as will-not-fix, whereas libzmq always sets TCP_NODELAY. The benchmark harness never set it. If you must use TCP, set NN_TCP_NODELAY=1 and re-measure.

Large payloads, peak throughput or many subscribers. ZeroMQ won these in the study: peak throughput was about 4.8 vs 3.8 GB/s in-process and 2.9 vs 1.7 GB/s over IPC, and 512 KB in-process latency was 86 vs 118 us. nanomsg funnels all async I/O through one worker thread.

Workloads that need delivery guarantees, backpressure or persistence on PUB/SUB. Delivery is best-effort, and messages are silently dropped when a subscriber or the TCP stack falls behind (#390). There is no broker and no shared-memory transport (#902).

Streaming many tiny messages through one inproc pipe as fast as possible. A 2014 report (#300) found PAIR inproc throughput about 4.5x slower than ZeroMQ (2.45 s vs 0.55 s), which contributors attributed to an eventfd signal per message.

integration.form: shared lib (default) or static lib (-DNN_STATIC_LIB=ON; Windows callers must also define NN_STATIC_LIB)
integration.dependencies: none beyond libc, POSIX pthreads and BSD sockets (Windows: ws2_32, mswsock, advapi32); CMake to build; asciidoctor optional for docs; also packaged in vcpkg and distro repos
integration.min_toolchain: ANSI C89 compiler; CMake 2.8.12+ (CMake 4.x supported since 1.2.2); Windows Vista+ with MSVC 2010+ (mingw-w64 untested)
integration.platforms: Linux, macOS, FreeBSD/NetBSD/OpenBSD, Solaris, HP-UX, QNX, Android and Windows per CMakeLists; CI covers Linux, Windows and macOS; architecture-independent C
integration.thread_safety: Sockets are designed to be safe to use from multiple threads, but upstream still discourages using one socket from several threads in parallel; all async I/O runs on a single internal worker thread
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: false — the C API (int sockets, nn_* calls, no context) and the SP wire protocol differ from libzmq/ZMTP, so it cannot replace libzmq in place or talk to ZeroMQ peers; the patterns map closely, so a port is mostly mechanical

gotchas: Filtering happens on the subscriber side. PUB sends every message to every connected SUB and the SUB's trie discards non-matches, so traffic nobody subscribed to still costs transport bandwidth and CPU.

NN_RCVMAXSIZE defaults to 1024 kB, so larger messages are refused on receive unless you raise it (-1 removes the limit). NN_MAX_SOCKETS is a build-time cap of 512 sockets per process, and inproc ignores NN_SNDBUF (the receiver's NN_RCVBUF sets the buffer).

Versions before 1.2.3 have a remotely exploitable buffer overflow in the WebSocket handshake (CVE-2026-97152, CVSS 4.0 score 8.6). 1.2.5 (2026-09) stopped malformed IPC headers from aborting the process. Distro packages such as the benchmarked 1.1.5 predate both fixes.
The 'nanomsg' name is a trademark, separate from the MIT code license. COPYING names Martin Sustrik as the owner and nanomsg.org names Garrett D'Amore.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick nanomsg over TCPSHM, a Linux-only, header-only, point-to-point channel with acked in-memory resend, when you need one-to-many PUB/SUB fan-out or Windows/macOS. Pick it over Mino, an IDL-typed zero-copy shared-memory framework, when you want a small, stable C library that sends untyped byte messages through a socket-style API. For raw same-host latency, TCPSHM's SHM mode (0.34 us RTT vs ZeroMQ IPC's 30.7 us) is in a different class.
verified_claims_summary: An independent Hitachi Energy study (IEEE SRDS 2025) compared nanomsg 1.1.5 with ZeroMQ (libzmq 4.3.4 + CZMQ 4.2.1) and NNG 1.9.0, using a gcc -O2 C harness against prebuilt distro packages (NNG built from source). The test was one-host PUB/SUB on a Xeon w3-2435 (8 cores, 64 GB), 5000 messages x 4 runs. With 1 subscriber at a 1000 us publish interval, nanomsg's mean latency at 1 KB was 7.5 vs 10.3 us in-process and 16.2 vs 25.8 us over IPC (about 1.4-1.6x, derived from the published CSV). The gap narrowed to about 1.1-1.2x at 32 KB and reversed at larger sizes, and ZeroMQ kept the best peak throughput and worst-case latency.
status_note: Active by commit date (1.2.5 released 2026-09-06), but officially in sustaining mode: only severe fixes are made and NNG is recommended for new work. It is MIT-licensed pure C that is easy to build via CMake or vcpkg, or to vendor.
